rules.note: Two rounds: an absolute majority of valid votes in the first round, otherwise a run-off between the top two four weeks later. Term of six years from 1994 and four years since the 2005 reform (first applied to the 2005 election); no immediate re-election.
Whole chamber every four years with the first presidential round since 2005 (2001 was a separate parliamentary election). Congress cannot be dissolved.
Eight-year terms; about half of the elected seats are renewed every four years by region.

historical.note: The first round was held on 12 December 1999, before the game starts (round 1 below); the run-off on 16 January 2000 (round 2). Lagos ran for the Concertación (PPD and PS); Lavín for the Alliance for Chile (UDI). Others in round 1: Sara Larraín (independent) 0.44% and Arturo Frei Bolívar (independent) 0.38%. Shares are of valid votes, computed from the SERVEL figures in the Wikipedia results table. Turnout 89.95% (first round) and 90.63% (run-off).
